title: Time Attack
text: “Motoyasu-san”
“What is it?”
Itsuki called out to me here.
“It’s a time attack, isn’t it? I won’t lose.”
“That’s my line.”

Since I’d already been through this once, I intended to go all out from the start. Just like last time—a swift strike, indeed. The longer this dragged on, the higher the chances of Rival showing up. In my head, I could almost hear Rival’s exasperated voice going, “Nano, why are you so convinced Gaelion’s gonna show up here, nano!?” But that was surely just my imagination. It should just go conquer that other world in peace, I say. In the end, maybe I’d vent my frustrations by sending Itsuki flying off somewhere, hm? Letting him live out a new life together with Mole was one option, indeed. The moment that thought crossed my mind, some other-loop version of Itsuki cried out in accusation, “We’ve basically become comrades-in-arms, and this is what you’re thinking on the inside!?” But was there really anything wrong with that? Sending him off to that other world and thinking of him as useful personnel there was also a valid option, I say. Though if I wasn’t careful, he might just end up boosting Rival’s fighting strength, so I’d have to think it over. Setting Rafumi-chan aside, wasn’t there anyone else amusing I could send flying? …Sending Rafumi-chan was still the best option. The problem was how exactly to send her flying.
While I was mulling this over, the Wave countdown hit zero. We were pulled into the Wave’s field, and a crack split open the sky.
“Here we go!”
“Let’s do this!”
“Daaaash!”
Yuki took off running, and Kou dashed forward carrying Itsuki. …In that other loop, Itsuki’s group had appeared nearby and pointed at me, brimming with hostility.
Tap tap! Itsuki, perched on Kou’s back—or rather his head—was already firing off bow skills. I couldn’t afford to fall behind here!
“Yuki-chan! Faster! Push forward, quickly!”
“Here we go! High Quick!”
Otherwise I’d lose to Itsuki.
“Kou’s going too~”
“Yes, run with everything you’ve got. We can’t lose to Motoyasu-san and Yuki-san. Ah… though maybe it would’ve been better to let that rabbit fellow run instead.”
“Why’s that?”
“Well, you’re a rabbit, aren’t you? Losing to a bird seems a bit sad. What’s the point of that big body and those legs if not for this?”
“You really do love provoking people…”
“Heh… or is it that you keep that big body of yours around just so Naofumi-san can hug you?”
Itsuki taunted Rabbit Guy with a fearless grin. Well, my own usaunny form existed purely so Father could pet and fluff me up, thank you very much.
“Just how sharp does that tongue of yours get!? Iwatani-sama did mention it, but you really do put your accuracy skill to full use, don’t you… right where it hurts.”
“Say whatever you like. So, is that body of yours really there just so Naofumi-san can hug you?”
“If we’re going there, what about you? The moment anything happens you’re climbing right onto Iwatani-sama. Don’t you think it’s about time you stopped being so clingy?”
Rabbit Guy and Itsuki traded insults as they trailed along behind me. Take your bickering elsewhere, I say.
“Honestly, shouldn’t you be the one cuddling up to Emia-san? Why do you glue yourself to Iwatani-sama the second anything happens?”
“That’s because staying near Naofumi-san makes it easier to spot this country’s… Trash.”
Itsuki grinned wickedly at that, and Rabbit Guy shook his head with a sigh.
“Not that I can’t understand the feeling. Honestly… I really wish this country’s mess would just wrap up already.”
“No matter how many of those self-important, so-called ‘superior beings’ of humanity we take down, more just keep sprouting up. Makes me want to throw up.”
“While you two are busy squabbling, I’ll go ahead and finish this in one push!”
It was nice being able to attack without holding back. Since Itsuki was on my side this time, as long as I didn’t aim wrong, there’d be no friendly fire.
“Liberation Firesquall X! Aiming Lancer X! Brionac X!”
“Oops! I don’t have time to keep dealing with him forever, do I! Arrow Rain X! Eagle Piercing Shot X! And then… Drifa Stone Shot X!”

As if trying to keep pace with my attacks, Itsuki unleashed a barrage of area attacks of his own. Caught in the combined wide-area skills and magic from the two of us, the monsters pouring out of the Wave’s crack were blown away in an instant, not a trace left behind.
“Oops, if I don’t hold back a little, won’t you have trouble securing the materials you want, Motoyasu-san?”
“True enough.”

Getting too into the competitive spirit, I’d blown all the materials to smithereens. So I switched to holding back my skills against the stray Wave monsters I’d missed—though the Wave boss still got one-shot, of course. There was absolutely no way I was letting Rival show up here, nooooooooooooo way!
“Itsuki! Don’t you dare blow away the boss!”
That would cut into the food I had to feed Fleon-chan.
“I know, I know. Though really… to think I got so full of myself over Wave battles this easy. It’s genuinely appalling. Isn’t it?”
Itsuki fired off a warning shot toward Rabbit Guy with a swish. Even though it was aimed to miss, Rabbit Guy still darted back to put some distance between them, glaring.
“What was that? You were just trying to hit me, weren’t you?”
“No? I could’ve hit you but I didn’t, see? Think of it as a friendly greeting.”
Itsuki’s twisted streak really knew no bounds.
“So, what do you think? Wasn’t my clownish foolishness back in that earlier Wave truly, spectacularly stupid? Come on, agree with me. Say it—‘You were an idiot, ahahaha!’”
“Iwatani-sama’s going to be upset, so if you don’t knock it off soon I’ll have to hold you down by force.”
“Sorry about that. Looking up at this sky just makes me feel like I’m being shown my own stupidity all over again—it’s incredibly frustrating.”
“Boo… if you don’t take this seriously everyone’s gonna get hurt, you know?”
At Kou’s words, Itsuki looked at him with the gentle eyes of someone doting on a child and patted his head.
“While Itsuki and the others are busy arguing, I’ll go ahead and take down the boss!”
“Ah, that’s already—”

Just as the Wave boss showed itself… an arrow abruptly dropped from the sky, piercing straight through it and finishing it off. When on earth had that arrow been fired? I wondered—but it seemed to be the very same shot Itsuki had launched high into the air right after we’d started running. Don’t tell me he’d fired it as a setup all along? Ngh… beaten to the punch by the likes of Itsuki. Frustrating as it was, if I spent time protesting, Rival might just poke her face out of the Wave’s crack, so I smoothly fired off Brionac at the rift and sealed it shut. I’m fairly sure we finished several seconds faster than the Wave we’d fought while staying in Melromarc. New time attack record, indeed! Rival! Stay over there in that other world forever, I saaaaay! Fuhahahahahahaha, indeed!
“Ah, it’s over? That ended really fast~”
“All we did was run~”
“Boooring~”
The Filolial-samas were all offering up their opinions together. At this rate, this Wave had become basically just routine busywork.
“Since I figured as much, I already arranged a race to see who’d finish first! Time for the rankings, indeed!”
“Hmph! Naturally!”
At this, Yuki-chan struck a pose out in front, still carrying me on her back. Of course, we were the ones in the lead.
“We already knew Yuki’d be first~”
“I wanted more obstacles and stuff~”
“Even a footrace ends fast—let’s play tag some more~”
“Sounds good. Round two, indeed!”
“Yaaay!”
And so, right then and there, a game of tag among the Filolial-samas got underway.
